title: NSW at the highest risk in looming bushfire season
full_text:
NSW is home to eight of Australia’s 10 highest-risk bushfire hotspots, with households being urged to prepare for a potentially scorching El Nino summer.
The South Coast and Central Coast will be among the nation’s most vulnerable regions this summer, with Batemans Bay, Gosford, Wyong and Shoalhaven occupying the top four positions on the list.
Forecasters warn the 2026-27 summer has the potential to be one of Australia’s hottest on record, with El Nino conditions raising concerns about increased bushfire danger across parts of eastern Australia.
The risk data from insurer GIO also ranked northwestern Sydney, including Blacktown, The Hills Shire and Penrith, prominently, the Hunter Valley and Blue Mountains.
The data identified postcodes covering Batemans Bay, Batehaven and Catalina, Gosford, Wyong, Huskisson, Vincentia and Sanctuary Point among the four highest-risk areas nationally.
Severe Weather Meteorologist Andrew Bufalino said the coming summer had the potential to bring extreme heat and heightened fire danger.
“There is the potential for a very hot summer across Australia, with an increased risk of extreme fire danger across parts of eastern Australia,” Mr Bufalino said.
“Should rainfall deficiencies return to areas that have recently experienced wetter conditions, fuel drying could accelerate rapidly under hot conditions, substantially increasing the risk of bushfire.
“Even in seasons where widespread bushfire activity is not expected, a single period of hot, dry and windy weather can still create significant localised impacts.“ He warned even in seasons where widespread bushfire activity was not expected, a single period of hot, dry and windy weather could still create significant localised impacts.
